statements.text: And then who is in charge at the Department of Defense at looking at the rules of the road for the incorporation of AI into, you know, into the Defense Department? [...] You know, do we legislate, do we regulate, do we think about it, is there a commission, do we want the flip phone generation regulating AI.
statements.context: Questioning witnesses during a House Armed Services Committee hearing on the Defense Intelligence Enterprise's posture in strategic competition with China.

statements.text: all of them would say that ChatGPT is one of the most ground shaking changes or innovations out there. [...] And they will rattle off a list of military implications of the commercial availability of that AI, right, putting it at someone's fingertips. [...] So I certainly know that you all have been focused on looking at other militaries and what they are incorporating in terms of AI, but who is in charge of looking at what the commercial availability of AI will mean for the U.S. military?
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing reviewing the Defense Intelligence Enterprise's posture and capabilities in strategic competition with China.

statements.text: And so how do we govern it? And our constituents are asking us, like, what are the ground rules on this new technology because it sounds scary? [...] But could you give us a sense, sort of in colloquial English, of what keeps you up at night about the military use of AI? If China is investing at least 3 times, and in some cases 10 times, the amount that we are, what is the number one thing that you feel like, you know, kind of worst-case scenario, if we go unchecked, we could see in the next decade?
statements.context: House hearing titled 'Man and Machine: Artificial Intelligence on the Battlefield,' where Representative Slotkin questions witnesses on military AI governance and the US-China investment gap.

statements.text: For the better part of 40 years, it has been taking on water, and now we are about to hit a category 5 hurricane in the form of artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence has the potential to change our economy more than the internet did. Think about that. [...] Productivity will go up, jobs will be gained, but jobs will also be lost. Maybe not Michigan jobs at first. Entry-level college jobs like paralegals or accountants are probably first on the list, but change is coming, and we need to be ready.
statements.context: Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) delivers her maiden speech on the Senate floor, outlining her policy priorities.

statements.text: What I am concerned about is that before we hardly know what is happening, we are going to let software decide if a veteran gets a benefit or not. [...] does the Legion have thinking on this?
statements.context: Senator Slotkin addresses a multi-VSO legislative presentation, raising AI in VA benefit decisions as a separate issue for the veterans' community to consider.

statements.text: how much power are we going to give to AI to decide if a veteran gets reimbursed for something, if a veteran qualifies for something. I just think we are moving very fast and there are some real benefits, I know, but a human being needs to be in the decision tree before we start making life-and-death decisions for veterans.
statements.context: Senator Slotkin delivers remarks during a joint hearing with veterans service organizations before a Senate committee.
